catalog_title: Real-World Vessel Forms: Working Reference Supplement
purpose: A source-backed, explicitly incomplete catalogue of real everyday and archaeological vessel examples to replace analytic test geometry as the design anchor. This is a reference index, not a reconstruction dataset or historical authenticity claim.

scope.priority: Everyday and archaeological references are recorded separately. Unknown is retained where a source was not found or does not report a feature.
not_in_scope: editing code or the 2026-10-04 reference catalog
claiming a full profile from a product photograph

evidence_contract.REPORTED_FACT: A field directly stated by the cited museum, archaeological archive, product maker, or retailer record. Unit and wording/source location are retained.
evidence_contract.CALCULATED_RATIO: Arithmetic from published measurements. It is a scale cue, not an additional measurement.
evidence_contract.VISUAL_INFERENCE: A broad observation based on the page's photographs or captions. It is not a measured profile, thickness, curvature, or foot dimension.
evidence_contract.DESIGN_ASSUMPTION: A provisional generator choice. It is not evidence about the cited physical object and must remain labeled as an assumption.
evidence_contract.UNKNOWN: Not stated in the reviewed source. Do not fill this field from an uncalibrated photograph.

workspace_support_snapshot.readme: vesselforge/README.md describes the first supported specimen as one open turned vessel with a swept, boolean-fused handle, and says later bowl/cup/plate/jar/bottle/jug models need sourced references.
workspace_support_snapshot.profile_catalog: vesselforge/src/vesselforge/profile_catalog.py exposes only bowl, beaker, and jar. Its module header calls the forms analytic starter candidates not matched to real vessels. The bowl foot-radius rule is a fixed fraction of max radius, not source-derived.
workspace_support_snapshot.geometry_model: No models.py was found. VesselSpec is in src/vesselforge/geometry.py: the current fixed prototype has body width 41 mm, height 56 mm, wall 4 mm and a swept handle; validation constrains width to 36–48 mm, height to 50–62 mm, and wall to 3.5–5 mm. These are prototype bounds, not measured vessel data.

family_coverage.generic_current_handle: A swept handle exists on the prototype, but the current shape is not a sourced handled-vessel family model.

family_coverage.best_use: Use Aberdeen for a contemporary footed daily bowl envelope/foot, Ame for explicit qualitative thinness, and IKEA for a larger daily scale. Met 18.56.44 is the clearest plain circular ceramic bowl with reported rim, foot, and height for a first rotational analog; Met 18.56.47 is a distinct lobed-rim type and should remain a separate future non-axisymmetric target. No cited source supplies a calibrated complete section.

candidate_bowl_design.purpose: A concrete first family candidate for a modern, small daily footed bowl, with its reported envelope and foot separated from the unmeasured profile and wall.

parameters.name: overall_plan_size_mm
parameters.candidate: 108 mm overall diameter for the small footed-bowl variant
parameters.evidence: Aberdeen City Museums reports overall height x diameter = 53 x 108 mm.
parameters.note: The source reports overall diameter, not separately rim diameter. A rotational generator may map 108 mm to its maximum opening/outer diameter as a DESIGN_ASSUMPTION. Ame provides another daily scale, W=D=120 mm, H55 mm; IKEA reports D160 mm, H70 mm.

parameters.name: overall_height_mm
parameters.evidence: Aberdeen City Museums reports overall height 53 mm.

parameters.name: height_to_plan_width_ratio
parameters.evidence: 53/108 from Aberdeen City Museums overall height and diameter.

parameters.name: foot_outer_diameter_mm
parameters.evidence: Aberdeen City Museums reports a 31 mm diameter foot ring on the same 53 x 108 mm bowl.
parameters.note: This is the foot-ring diameter only; foot height and section remain UNKNOWN. Met 18.56.47 independently reports a historical foot diameter of 70 mm on a 191 mm rim (ratio 0.3665), a visibly different proportion.

parameters.name: wall_thickness_mm
parameters.candidate: UNKNOWN; leave unset until object measurement or section/scan exists
parameters.evidence: Time & Style calls its separate Ame bowl thin, but Aberdeen gives no wall measurement or thin-wall statement. The Aberdeen photo's light-looking rim is VISUAL_INFERENCE only.

parameters.name: foot_height_and_section
parameters.evidence: No selected target source reports it.

parameters.name: inner_and_outer_meridian
parameters.candidate: UNKNOWN; a smooth axisymmetric curve from rounded lower body to outward-rising rim would be a DESIGN_ASSUMPTION for a prototype
parameters.evidence: Aberdeen photographs show a rounded footed bowl silhouette, but no published calibrated side profile is supplied.

candidate_bowl_design.guardrail: Do not label a generated meridian as an exact Aberdeen object reconstruction. Its overall height, overall diameter, and foot-ring diameter are reported facts; rim mapping, rotational symmetry, curve control points, foot section, and any numeric wall offset remain DESIGN_ASSUMPTION or UNKNOWN. Ame and IKEA provide separate everyday size variants, not evidence for Aberdeen's section.

source_review_notes.open_access: Met selected pages identify Public Domain and Met Open Access usage. Apsida item metadata states CC BY-SA 4.0 for its OBJ resource. Aberdeen page result states image copyright © Chris Keenan. Commercial product page imagery has no open license identified in this pass.
source_review_notes.image_scan_handling: No image, OBJ, CAD, or mesh downloaded. Image counts are not treated as multi-view geometric coverage. The Apsida OBJ is listed in metadata but not locally inspected.
source_review_notes.evidence_boundary: Reported dimensions support envelopes and ratios only. Photographs are not used to estimate unreported wall thickness, foot diameter, rim section, base curvature, neck diameter, handle section, or precise control points.
